To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
isolated rat renal tubules synthesize guanidinoacetate from arginine and/or canavanine and L-glycine.
isolated rat renal tubules synthesized guanidino acetic acid from arginine or its analog, canavanine and L-glycine.

guanidinobutyrate is synthesized from arginine, canavanine, and glycine in the isolated renal tubules from rat kidney and creatine is a negative feedback inhibitor for the synthesis of guanidinohybutyrate in the renal tubules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biosynthesis of guanidinopropionate from arginine or argininosuccinate, glycine and ATP in the presence of the enzymes arginine transaminase and arginine succinic acid lyase.
the regulation of guanidinopropionic acid synthesis in isolated rat tubule.
the mechanism of guanidinopropionate biosynthesis from arginine and glycin in rat kidneys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
guanidinacetate synthesis in rat kidney tubules occurs only via the amidotransferase pathway.

the synthesis of guanidinosuccinic acid from arginine and glycin in isolated rat kidney tubules is mediated by the enzyme glycine transamidinase, and that the synthesis is inhibited by creatine, but not by hydroxyurea or by the guanidine derivatives of argininosuccinate and arginine.
guanidinotransferases (transamidases) are present in the renal tubule, and that they are responsible for guanidinoacetate synthesis from arginine and/or canavanine and from glycine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
creatine synthesis is regulated by creatine and guanidinoacetate in rat renal tubules.

guanidinotransferases (transamidases) are localized in the proximal convoluted tubules, and that the rate of guanidinocarboxylic acid synthesis is regulated by the availability of glycine, the rate of creatine synthesis, and the concentration of the end products of the guanidine and urea cycles.

guanidinoglycine, guanidinoglucose, guanidinoacetate and creatine are synthesized from arginine, glycine and glucose in isolated renal tubules, but the guanidine and creatine cycles may not function fully.
The main takeaway from our work is that
guanidinopropionic acid is synthesized from arginine, canavanine or norvaline and glycine.
the guanidino group of creatine is not derived from the urea cycle.
guanidinopropionate is synthesized by a transamidinase in the renal tubule and is a precursor for the guanidine group in the guanidino compounds creatine, creatinine and arginine.
